---
title: "Configuration"
guide-section: "Reference"
---

What a dataset is made of on disk, what `tether.toml` can say, and where
credentials and other per-checkout settings live.

## Layout

```
<dataset-root>/
  tether.toml                 # committed: tether.version (older -> `tether upgrade`), dataset.id (the namespace
                              #   of this dataset's refs), snapshot.auto, verify.on_status,
                              #   new.fork (lazy|eager), default policies, non-secret backend options
  .tether/
    .gitignore                # ignores workspace.toml, ops.jsonl, secrets.toml, cache/, lock
    secrets.toml              # untracked: everything a clone must not decide -- credentials or references,
                              #   endpoints, executables, init SQL; per kind, per URI prefix, per object
    objects/<key>.toml        # committed, one per object: kind, locator, policy, state, pin,
                              #   recoverable, captured_at, origin (only when "created")
    listings/<hash>.jsonl     # committed, content-addressed per-file listings for directory/prefix
                              #   states (so `diff --content` can compare them); pruned by gc
    workspace.toml            # untracked: workspace_id, bookmark, working refs, pending forks, base states, fork points, last snapshot
    ops.jsonl                 # untracked: the operation log -- each store-writing command, what it did, what it replaced

<vcs shared dir>/           # .jj/repo/ or .git/ -- one per clone, shared by every checkout, never committed
  tether.lock                 # the repository-wide lock (commit, pull, gc, drop, abandon, undo, new hold it)
  tether-pinned.jsonl         # pins this clone created (commit, repair): the only ones `gc` releases without
                              #   --release-foreign; seeded from the op logs the first time gc needs it
  tether-created.jsonl        # stores this clone created with `add --create`: dataset id, kind, identity,
                              #   locator, key, when, the bookmark it was made on -- what `gc --delete-stores`
                              #   may delete once nothing references them
  tether-touched.jsonl        # stores this clone forked a branch in or pinned: where `gc` looks for this
                              #   dataset's dead refs once no manifest names the store any more
```

The indexes live with the repository rather than in history or a checkout
on purpose: an abandoned fork takes with it the manifest that named the
store, and `forget-workspace` takes the checkout's own files; the memory of
what tether made, pinned, and wrote has to survive both. They are only
memories -- the owner marker the backend wrote into the store decides whose
the store is (see [Reclaiming Storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd)).

`pin_id = <dataset-id>.<blake2b(kind, locator identity, content state)[:16]>`;
the native ref is `tether.<pin_id>`. Identical state yields the same pin within
a dataset, so re-committing an unchanged object is a no-op and identical states
dedupe to one pin; the dataset id keeps `gc` inside its own namespace when
several datasets pin one store.

## `tether.toml`

A dataset's configuration is `tether.toml` at the dataset root, committed with
the manifests and loaded into `RepoConfig`. Every key but `[dataset] id` has a
default; a minimal file is `[tether] version = 4` plus the id `init` generates.
A dataset whose version is older than this tether's is refused by every
command except `tether upgrade`, which brings it forward in one step (see the
[CLI Guide](07-cli.qmd#upgrade)).

```toml
[tether]
version = 4         # the format this tether writes; older datasets need `tether upgrade`

[dataset]
id = "0a1b2c3d"      # 8 hex chars; the namespace of this dataset's pins and branches in every store

[snapshot]
auto = false         # `status` shows the last snapshot (--snapshot refreshes); true: fingerprint on every status

[verify]
on_status = false    # also run a cheap verify of each committed object in status

[new]
fork = "lazy"        # "lazy": create a working branch on first writable open; "eager": during `new`

[defaults]           # policy for objects added without an explicit one
file = "immutable"   # immutable | versioned
pin = "native"       # native | record

[vcs]
prefer = "jj"        # which adapter to use when both .jj and .git exist
trunk = "main"       # the bookmark that stands for every object's upstream branch

[backends.file]      # non-secret options only; one table per kind (see "Trust boundary")
storage_options = { region = "us-west-2" }
```

## Dataset id

`init` generates `[dataset] id`; `tether.toml` is committed, so every clone
shares it. Every native ref carries it -- pins `tether.<id>.<hash>`, working
branches `tether.ws.<id>.<bookmark>` -- and `gc` stays inside that
namespace, so datasets can share one Icechunk repo or Neon project without
being able to delete each other's pins. Datasets from before the id existed get
one from `tether upgrade`.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not change the id after committing

- Pins and branches made under the old id stop being this dataset's: `gc`
  treats them as foreign and leaves them alone.
- `repair` recreates the pins the manifests name, under the new id.
- A fork meant to become an *independent* dataset must change the id *before*
  it pins anything, or the two share a namespace and can `gc` each other.
:::

## Policies

A `Policy` is stored per object (`[policy]` in its manifest), set with the
`--file` and `--pin` options of `tether add` (or `Repo.add(policy=...)`)
and changed in place with `tether set KEY... --file|--pin`. Whether writes
fork a branch or land on the upstream branch is not a policy: it is which
bookmark the working copy is on (the trunk writes upstream; any other
bookmark forks). Manifests from before 0.1.0a9 carry a `write` key; it is read
and ignored, and `tether upgrade` drops it.

| Field | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `immutable` (default), `versioned` | `file` backend only. `immutable`: any drift is an error at `status`. `versioned`: a single object in a versioning-enabled bucket/container is Addressable through its version id. |
| `pin` | `native` (default), `record` | Any backend. `record` drops `PIN`: `commit` records the state without creating a native ref, and `new` forks straight from the recorded state. Cheaper (no tag/branch per commit, nothing for `gc` to release) but recoverable only while the system retains that state -- `verify` reports `missing` once it is gone. See [Reclaiming Storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd). |

## Import query

`[import] query` in `.tether/secrets.toml` is the default SQL for
`tether import` when neither `--table` nor `--query` is given. It must yield
tether's canonical columns (`key`, `kind`, `uri` / `locator_json`, optional
`policy_*`, `at`), and runs as one statement in a read-only transaction; the
source (DSN or file) is still passed on the command line. The committed
`tether.toml` may not set it (see the trust boundary below): `import` refuses
one there and names where it goes. See
[Registries and SQL](10-registries-and-sql.qmd).

```toml
# .tether/secrets.toml
[import]
query = "SELECT 'zarr/' || name AS key, 'icechunk' AS kind, uri FROM catalog WHERE format = 'icechunk'"
```

## Backend options

`[backends.<kind>]` is handed to the backend when it is first used. Only what
a backend allowlists may be set in the committed file -- `storage_options` for
`file`/`delta`/`lance`, `catalog` for `iceberg` -- and inside those tables only
the keys the backend names (`region`, `allow_http`,
`virtual_hosted_style_request`, `conditional_put`; `type`, `warehouse`,
`name`). Any other key is refused by name: an allowlist, so an option tether
has never heard of cannot reach a store from a clone. Everything else goes in
`.tether/secrets.toml` (next section), where the same tables may hold any key.
The per-backend keys are listed in [Backends](09-backends.qmd).

## Trust boundary: `.tether/secrets.toml` {#trust-boundary-tethersecretstoml}

A cloned dataset is untrusted input. `tether.toml` and the manifests arrive
with every clone, so nothing in them may choose an executable tether runs, an
endpoint your credentials are sent to, SQL to execute, or which environment
variable holds a secret. tether refuses a committed `tether.toml` that tries
(`[vcs] git_path`, `[import] query`, `[backends.neon] api_url`,
`[backends.ducklake] init_sql`, a `storage_options.endpoint`, ...) and says
where the key belongs. What that adds up to is the
[security model](#security-model) below.

Those settings live in `.tether/secrets.toml` -- untracked, per checkout,
never committed -- or in the environment:

```toml
[vcs]
git_path = "/usr/bin/git"                 # or TETHER_GIT / TETHER_JJ in the environment
# jj_path = "/opt/jj/bin/jj"

[backends.neon]                           # per-kind options the committed file may not set
api_key_env = "NEON_API_KEY"

[backends.ducklake]
init_sql = ["CREATE SECRET (TYPE S3, PROVIDER credential_chain)"]

[uris."s3://lab-a-bucket/"]               # every object whose store URI starts here
profile = "lab-a"                          # an AWS shared-config profile ...
# role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/lab-a"   # ... or a role, assumed via STS ...
# access_key_id = "..."                    # ... or, when nothing else will do, literal keys
# secret_access_key = "..."
# endpoint_url = "http://seaweedfs.local:8333"

[objects."zarr/imaging"]                  # one object; beats a URI prefix
profile = "imaging"

[uris."mysql://dolt.internal:3306"]       # a Dolt server: the only one sent this password
user = "svc"                              #   (Dolt reads server entries only; an [objects.*]
password_env = "DOLT_PASSWORD"            #   entry does not reach it)

[import]                                  # the default SQL for `tether import`
query = "SELECT name AS key, 'file' AS kind, uri FROM catalog"
```

Resolution per object, first match wins: `[objects."<key>"]`, then the
longest matching `[uris."<prefix>"]`, then `[backends.<kind>]`, then the
environment and instance credential chain -- which is exactly today's
behaviour for an object with no entry. A `profile` or `role_arn` is resolved
through `boto3` (install it when you use them) into explicit credentials, so
two stores with two identities work in one command; `file`, `delta`, and
`lance` take the same entries as storage options; `icechunk` passes them to
`s3_storage` instead of reading the environment. Dolt is the exception: it
honours only the server's `[uris."mysql://host:port"]` entry (or one for
`mysql://host:port/database`), never an `[objects.*]` entry or the kind
section, because the manifest chooses the host the password is sent to.

The file may hold literal credentials, so tether warns when it is readable by
other users (`chmod 600`) and never prints its contents -- not in `status`,
not in `--json`, not in an error. `init` lists it in `.tether/.gitignore`;
`Repo.find` re-adds the entry if an older dataset lacks it.

### Advanced: two stores, two identities

The case the per-URI and per-object entries exist for. A dataset tracks an
Icechunk repository in the imaging lab's account and another in the
sequencing core's; each account issues its own credentials, and one
`commit` fingerprints and pins both. With `from_env` alone that is an
`AWS_PROFILE` switch between commands, which a single `commit` cannot do.

```bash
tether add zarr/imaging s3://imaging-lab-data/plate-01.icechunk --kind icechunk
tether add zarr/reads   s3://seqcore-archive/run-2026-09.icechunk --kind icechunk
```

```toml
# .tether/secrets.toml (this checkout only; never committed)
[uris."s3://imaging-lab-data/"]      # every object in the imaging bucket
profile = "imaging-lab"              # a profile in ~/.aws/config

[objects."zarr/reads"]               # one object, whichever bucket it is in
role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/seqcore-reader"
region = "us-east-2"
```

`tether commit` now opens `zarr/imaging` with the `imaging-lab` profile's
keys and `zarr/reads` with a session assumed into the sequencing core's role,
in the same process, with no environment change between them. Each entry is
resolved through `boto3` when the object is first touched; a third object
with no entry keeps using the ambient environment. The manifests record only
the two URIs -- the identities never leave this checkout.

On CI the same layout works with literal keys injected by the runner:

```toml
[uris."s3://imaging-lab-data/"]
access_key_id = "${IMAGING_KEY_ID}"      # a template your CI expands before
secret_access_key = "${IMAGING_SECRET}"  # writing the file; tether reads values
```

(tether does not expand `${...}` itself; write the file with the values in
place, or use a profile / role and let the runner's identity assume it.)

## Security model

What a cloned dataset -- its `tether.toml`, its manifests and history, and
every other file in the checkout -- can and cannot make tether do.

It cannot:

- **Run a program.** Executables come from `secrets.toml` or the
  environment. git runs with `core.fsmonitor`, hooks, and `ext::` transports
  off, and never takes a directory for a bare repository by itself. A `git`
  object's `path` must be absolute and outside the checkout, whose files came
  with the clone.
- **Send your credentials somewhere.** Endpoints are refused in committed
  files (the trust boundary above), and a Dolt password goes only to a server
  `secrets.toml` lists.
- **Run SQL.** `[import] query` and `init_sql` come from `secrets.toml` or the
  command line, and an import query runs as one statement in a read-only
  transaction.
- **Push your code.** A manifest's git `remote` must name a remote the
  repository already has.
- **Write outside `.tether/`.** Object keys are checked when a manifest is
  read, not only at `add`: no `..`, no `\`, no drive letters.

It can:

- **Name stores.** A locator is an address. A manifest can point `status`,
  `commit`, and `verify` at any store your ambient credentials reach, and
  they sign the requests (a signature does not reveal the secret). `commit`
  records what it finds there, a directory's file names and hashes
  included, and pushing publishes that.
- **Release pins in your stores.** `gc` releases the pins in its dataset's
  namespace that its own history does not reference and that its clone
  created; with `--release-foreign`, any of them. A clone that reuses your
  dataset id and names your stores can then release yours.
- **Make commands fail.** Every refusal above is an error: a hostile clone
  can stop a command, not redirect it.

So read a clone's manifests before its first `commit`, and a `gc` plan
before applying it.

## Workspace state

`.tether/workspace.toml` is untracked (ignored by the `.tether/.gitignore` that
`init` writes, alongside the operation log `.tether/ops.jsonl`) and is per
checkout / per jj workspace:

```toml
workspace_id = "7c1e0a4d9b2e4f6a8c1d3e5f7a9b0c2d"
bookmark = "relabel"                 # the dataset bookmark this checkout works on (absent: read-only)
last_snapshot_at = "2026-09-04T22:10:03.118Z"

[working_refs]                       # branches that exist (on the trunk: the upstream branches)
"zarr/imaging" = "tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel"
"db/metrics" = "tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel"

[pending_forks]                      # decided by `new`, created on first writable open
"features" = "tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel"

[pending_resets."features"]          # the head `new` reviewed and agreed to reset on that open
version = 9                          #   (a branch that moved since is refused instead)

[base_states."zarr/imaging"]         # committed state this working ref corresponds to
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"     #   (differs from the manifest => stale)

[fork_points."zarr/imaging"]         # base state when the branch was forked (for promote)
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"

[last_snapshot."zarr/imaging"]
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"
```

`base_states` drive stale-working-copy detection (per object); `working_refs`
are what `open` writes to; `pending_forks` are the branches `new` decided on but has not
created (the first writable `open` moves an entry to `working_refs`);
`pending_resets` record the head `new` saw on a branch it will reset, so a
writable `open` never resets a branch that moved in between; `last_snapshot`
(and `last_snapshot_at`) is what a plain `status` shows.

## Operation log

`.tether/ops.jsonl`, next to `workspace.toml` and equally untracked: one JSON
line per store-writing command, appended only (an interruption loses at most
the line being written). `tether ops` reads it, `tether undo` reverses from
it. Deleting it loses nothing but the ability to undo what came before. What
each entry holds, and how the journal survives an interrupted command:
[The operation log](07-cli.qmd#the-operation-log) in the CLI Guide.

## Environment variables

Every variable tether reads -- `TETHER_REV`, `TETHER_JJ` / `TETHER_GIT`,
`TETHER_PUBLISH_DSN`, `NEON_API_KEY`, the Dolt `*_env` names, the cloud
credential chains -- is in one table in the
[CLI Guide](07-cli.qmd#versions-and-environment), with the `GIT_*` variables
tether ignores.
